note:
FEATURE / WATER RENDERING / VOXEL ENGINE INTEGRATION ISSUE: Integrate the newly added stylized water shader package into the production voxel-engine water rendering path, and create a dedicated `WaterRenderingShowcase` scene that proves the reusable implementation across the water situations the game needs. The new shader is not merely a lookdev/reference asset: it should become the default presentation for all game water rendered through the standard voxel engine.

SOURCE ASSETS: The supplied package is currently under `Assets/Stylized Water Shader/`, including `Shaders/Stylized Water.shadergraph`, supporting shader subgraphs/HLSL, the provided material, foam/normal textures, Gerstner-wave displacement support, and related scripts. Treat this package as the visual/technical source to integrate. Do not leave the production game on the legacy water shader while only demonstrating the new shader on an isolated Unity plane.

ENGINE OWNERSHIP / ARCHITECTURE: Production ownership belongs in the reusable `VoxelEngine` rendering/water layer (and shared Game/WorldBuilder composition only where semantic configuration belongs). The existing voxel water generation, water-surface discovery/meshing, streaming, semantic material IDs, visibility controls, and diagnostics should continue to be the canonical geometry/gameplay path. Replace the presentation/material/shader path beneath that shared water abstraction so any world authored with standard voxel water automatically receives the new water rendering.

The showcase scene may select semantic water profiles and arrange examples, but it must not implement a second scene-local water renderer, manually maintain bespoke water meshes, depend on hand-authored planes as the production proof, fork the shader per scene, or bypass the normal voxel water data path. If the new shader needs additional reusable inputs such as flow direction, depth/shallow-water information, foam masks, shoreline/intersection data, wave parameters, or per-body profile values, add those as general water-rendering semantics/data contracts in the engine and feed them through the standard production path.

GLOBAL REPLACEMENT REQUIREMENT: After this work, existing game scenes that render water through the standard engine path—including `VoxelShowcase`, `KentridgePlayableSlice`, and future WorldBuilder-authored scenes—must use the new stylized water presentation without scene-by-scene material replacement. There must be one canonical production water presentation path. Legacy lookdev/test shaders may remain only when they are explicitly isolated diagnostic/reference assets; no normal game water should silently continue using the legacy production water material/shader.

NEW WATER RENDERING SHOWCASE: Add `Assets/Scenes/WaterRenderingShowcase.unity` and include it in the normal build/harness path. Build the showcase itself through the standard WorldBuilder/voxel-engine water authoring systems so it proves the exact production rendering path rather than a synthetic Shader Graph demo. The scene should be walkable and visually organized into clearly readable water cases under consistent lighting.

At minimum the showcase must demonstrate:
- a broad still/deep-water pool or lake area where large-scale wave motion, surface readability, transparency/color and distant viewing can be judged;
- a shallow shoreline where depth/color transition, water/terrain intersection, foam or shoreline treatment, and edge stability are easy to inspect;
- a flowing stream/river with an obvious directional flow profile distinct from the still-water case;
- a waterfall or steep flowing-water case with visibly appropriate directional motion and foam/surface breakup;
- water viewed adjacent to voxel cliffs/rocks/structures so depth, intersection, sorting and contact artifacts can be inspected;
- enough near-player and elevated views to judge both close material quality and large water-body behavior.

The showcase should expose reusable profile differences such as still/lake, river/stream and waterfall/rapid behavior through engine-level configuration rather than separate scene shaders. Exact profile names are implementation-defined, but they must be semantic reusable concepts.

VISUAL TARGET: Preserve the attractive characteristics of the supplied stylized shader—animated wave/normal breakup, readable deep/mid/shallow color variation, foam, directional flow, surface highlights/refraction/depth behavior where supported by the current render pipeline, and Gerstner-style displacement or equivalent surface motion—while adapting it correctly to the voxel engine's production water geometry and URP pipeline. Do not downgrade it to a flat blue transparent material merely to make integration easy.

SHORE / FOAM / DEPTH SEMANTICS: The production implementation must obtain shoreline/depth/foam behavior from reusable water/terrain information or robust render-pipeline inputs, not from hand-painted data that only works in the showcase. Where the supplied Shader Graph assumes inputs that the voxel renderer does not currently provide, add the smallest reusable engine capability needed. Foam should appear where it is semantically/visually justified (shore contact, rapid/waterfall turbulence, or equivalent) rather than uniformly covering every surface.

ANIMATION / FLOW: Water motion must be visibly animated in the built application. Still water, river flow and waterfall flow must not all read as the same panning texture with different colors. Direction and speed should come from reusable water profile/body data or an equivalent semantic flow contract. The implementation must remain deterministic/configurable and must not require per-scene shader edits.

INTERACTION / GAMEPLAY COMPATIBILITY: Do not break existing water collision, buoyancy, swimming/wading, voxel edits, water discovery, streaming, render-disable diagnostics, or other gameplay/runtime behavior while replacing presentation. If character/object disturbance or displacement is already part of the intended new water presentation path, integrate it through a reusable engine interaction contract rather than a showcase-only script. At minimum, the new rendering path must coexist correctly with player traversal and existing water gameplay semantics.

BUILD / SHADER RELIABILITY: The shader, Shader Graph dependencies, textures, variants and runtime material setup must survive real player builds. Do not rely on editor-only asset lookup or an accidental scene reference to prevent shader stripping. Integrate with the project's existing URP configuration rather than replacing the whole project render pipeline with package-specific pipeline assets unless a repository-wide pipeline change is explicitly proven necessary. The exact built application must render the new water without pink/missing materials, compile errors or missing variants.

PERFORMANCE / SCALE: This replaces all game water, so measure GPU/CPU cost, overdraw/transparent sorting impact, draw calls/batching, shader variant count, memory, water-mesh streaming interaction and large-body cost against existing device budgets. Preserve culling/visibility behavior and avoid per-water-voxel GameObjects or per-surface unique materials. A visually richer shader is acceptable only if it remains suitable as the default production path.

VISUAL INSPECTION IS REQUIRED: This ticket may not close from source inspection, shader compilation, unit tests, material-name assertions or a single static screenshot. The exact built `WaterRenderingShowcase` must be inspected in motion, and at least one existing production game scene containing water must also be built/launched and visually checked to prove the global replacement is actually active outside the showcase.

ACCEPTANCE:
(1) A new built `WaterRenderingShowcase` scene exists, is included in the normal scene/build harness, launches without startup/runtime exceptions, and is authored through standard WorldBuilder/voxel-engine water systems rather than hand-authored production water planes.
(2) The showcase contains clearly inspectable still/deep water, shallow shoreline, flowing river/stream, and waterfall/rapid cases, plus water touching representative voxel terrain/rock/structure geometry.
(3) All showcase cases use the same canonical reusable production water renderer with semantic/profile configuration; they are not separate scene-specific shader/material forks.
(4) `Assets/Stylized Water Shader/Shaders/Stylized Water.shadergraph` and its required support assets are integrated or appropriately promoted/adapted into the production voxel-engine water presentation path, preserving the supplied shader's intended stylized wave, color/depth, foam, flow and surface-detail character.
(5) Standard voxel-engine water in existing game scenes automatically uses the new presentation with no scene-by-scene material reassignment. Verify this in at least `VoxelShowcase` and one additional production scene with water (prefer `KentridgePlayableSlice` if it currently contains/encounters water).
(6) No normal game water remains on a legacy production water shader/material path. Any retained older water lookdev/test shader is explicitly diagnostic/reference-only and cannot be selected accidentally by normal world composition.
(7) Scene code contains only water placement/profile/configuration intent. Reusable material selection, shader binding, flow/depth/foam inputs, render data, batching/culling, and presentation behavior live in shared `VoxelEngine`/Game systems.
(8) Still, river and waterfall cases show visibly different appropriate motion in the built application through reusable flow/profile semantics; motion is not a static material and not implemented by per-scene shader edits.
(9) Shoreline/depth/foam treatment is robust on voxel-authored terrain contacts and derives from reusable production data/rendering semantics rather than showcase-only painted masks or coordinates.
(10) Existing water gameplay/runtime semantics—including collision/buoyancy/swimming or wading where applicable, streaming, water discovery/meshing, voxel edits, and diagnostic water visibility toggles—continue to function after the rendering replacement.
(11) The new shader and all required variants/resources work in the real player build with no pink materials, compile errors, editor-only dependencies or accidental shader stripping.
(12) Focused behavioral regressions exercise the real production water-material/shader selection path and prove that multiple independently authored water bodies/profiles route through the new canonical renderer. Source-string or material-name checks alone are insufficient.
(13) Add a portability regression or small production-authored test world that creates at least two water bodies with different profile/flow configuration and proves both use the shared path without `WaterRenderingShowcase` code.
(14) Durable visual evidence from the exact built `WaterRenderingShowcase` includes near-player and wider views of each required case plus time-separated frames or video-equivalent evidence showing animation/flow. Also capture built evidence from at least one existing game scene proving the replacement is active there.
(15) Direct visual review confirms the new water meets the repository quality bar: convincing large-body readability, stable shoreline contact, useful depth/color separation, localized foam where appropriate, coherent directional flow, no obvious transparent-sorting catastrophes, no floating/disconnected water surfaces, and no placeholder-quality fallback.
(16) Measure blast radius and CPU/GPU/memory/rendering cost for replacing all game water, including transparent overdraw, shader complexity/variants, draw calls/batching, culling, large water bodies and waterfall/foam cases; do not weaken existing device budgets to make the feature pass.
